Aetius suspended, but the same lines say Leontius kept favoring him ('soon reversed'); Aetius was a deacon, not a church head or prelate.

The cited lines show questioning at Aquileia and Ambrose's sermon line 'Auxentius is cast out', a declaration, not a removal carried out. The Aquileia sentence deposing Palladius is a council act already carried as major on the Aquileian link (P2-ML ruling on duplicates).
Paul of Samosata's deposition is the Antiochene synod's act, carried on the Anatolian link; this link is the synod's letter to Rome (P2-ML duplicates ruling).
Origen's deposition: Origen was a priest and teacher, not a church head or prelate, and the act belongs to Demetrius's third-century see, not the later Coptic side.
The 754 council cursed John of Damascus, a monk-priest, not a prelate; P2-ML treats it as a duplicate of the curse on the iconophile link.
Hilary's exile is mentioned as his past, imposed by neither side of this link (Gregory of Tours on Hilary's help to Clovis).
Hilary's return from exile is a date marker; the exile is not by the other side of the link.
Athanasius 'in exile from Alexandria' is background to Marcella's hearing of Antony; neither side of the link exiled him.
The Admonition's authors were imprisoned in 1572, but they were ministers, not church heads or prelates.
Familists imprisoned by the bishop of Norwich: lay members, not prelates.
Wesley on the ejection of Puritan ministers: not prelates, and not an act of the other side of the link.
Avvakum was an archpriest, not a prelate, and the link runs from the Old Believers as critics; no deposition by the Old Believers is shown.
Poland's 1658 expulsion of the Brethren is a group's exclusion by a third party (the Polish state), not by the Remonstrant side, and no prelate is involved.
Origen 'removed from Alexandria to Caesarea' means he moved; no deposition is shown in the link's sources.

On that test the Kievan links byzantine-imperial-church-macedonian--kievan-rus-christianity and kievan-rus-christianity--kievan-rus-christianity-1054-1240 go Thin, though Franklin and Shepard (1996) and Shepard's Cambridge History chapter are cited on the Rus' movements generally. If Mark reads 'supports the same reading' to include a movement-level standard history, those two (and possibly byzantine-church-after-1054--kievan-rus-christianity-1054-1240) would stay DMR with Franklin and Shepard added.

Three upward or confirming finds rest on story-level citations whose notes are topical, not page-level: Morris 1995 for the Lavra's founding by Phokas ('patrons, property, holy men'), Franklin and Shepard ch. 7 for the Studite rule at Kyiv ('On the Caves Monastery'), and Oleksa and Black for the 1794 Alaska mission. I have not seen these books; they are cited, as the brief allows, from the repo's own descriptions. The secondary entries carry no page or chapter beyond what the repo gives.
